detailed_analysis:
### Objective and Analytical Framework

The goal of this proposed analysis is to locate a sputtered gold (Au) layer within a spectral X-ray transmission dataset and to quantify its thickness using the characteristic Au K-edge absorption jump. According to authoritative tabulations (e.g., NIST XCOM), the Au K-edge lies at approximately 80.7 keV (80.725 keV); this value should be adopted for any quantitative work, since the thickness quantification depends on both the exact edge position and the tabulated jump in the mass attenuation coefficient (Δμ/ρ) across it. The measurement was performed with a Hexitec spectral X-ray detector over an 80 × 80 pixel grid (20 × 20 mm field of view, 0.25 mm spatial resolution), producing a full transmitted X-ray spectrum (2048 energy bins) at every pixel. A companion flat-field (I0) reference cube—acquired on the identical grid without any sample present—was supplied to enable conversion of raw transmitted counts into physically meaningful absorbance.

### The Role of the Flat-Field Reference

The supplied I0 baseline is essential to this measurement. In principle, the spatially averaged I0 spectrum should show the characteristic shape of a bremsstrahlung X-ray source: a steep low-energy rise, a broad continuum, and sharp characteristic emission lines from the tube target (e.g., tungsten K-lines near ~59 and ~67 keV) superimposed on the continuum. The exact spectral shape—including the endpoint energy set by the tube voltage and the position of any characteristic lines—has not been verified here, because the I0 spectrum is not shown. This verification matters: for a source with sufficient tube voltage, bremsstrahlung must extend above the 80.7 keV Au K-edge to provide usable flux in the above-edge window; the available flux in that window is a key determinant of feasibility and must be confirmed from the actual spectrum rather than assumed.

Dividing the sample spectrum by this baseline (and taking the negative logarithm) is intended to isolate the attenuation caused by the sample alone, converting instrument-and-source-dependent raw counts into an absorbance signal in which an element's absorption edges appear as steps. One caveat requires attention: the tungsten characteristic K-lines (~59 and ~67 keV) sit relatively close to the Au K-edge window and could complicate normalization if their subtraction is imperfect; the claim that the edge window is 'free' of source structure therefore needs to be checked against the measured I0 spectrum rather than assumed.

### Locating the Gold (Proposed Approach)

Gold would be identified spatially by searching for pixels that exhibit a discrete increase in absorption as the X-ray energy crosses ~80.7 keV. Just below the edge, X-rays pass through gold relatively easily; just above the edge, a new atomic absorption channel (ejection of a K-shell electron) opens abruptly, increasing attenuation. Mapping the magnitude of this step across the field of view would, in principle, produce a spatial map of gold presence: pixels with a strong edge jump would correspond to regions where the sputtered layer is present, while pixels with negligible jump would correspond to bare substrate or background. This edge-difference approach is attractive because the ~80.7 keV K-edge is a fingerprint unique to gold and is distinct in energy from the source emission lines at lower energies. No edge-jump map has yet been produced or verified, so the ability to cleanly localize gold remains a hypothesis pending actual data.

### Quantifying Thickness (Proposed Approach)

Once a gold-bearing region is identified, thickness could be derived from the size of the edge jump. The height of the absorbance step at the K-edge is expected to be proportional to the areal amount (mass per unit area) of gold along the X-ray path, following the Beer–Lambert relationship: the change in absorbance across the edge equals the difference in gold's mass attenuation coefficient (above minus below the edge) multiplied by the gold areal density. Because Δμ/ρ across the Au K-edge is a tabulated physical constant, converting a measured edge-jump map into a thickness map would require only knowledge of gold's bulk density.

The edge-ratio method has a useful property for thin films: taking the ratio of transmission just above and just below the edge cancels slowly varying contributions from other materials and from the beam profile. However, this cancellation is only partial and should not be described as fully self-calibrating. Energy-dependent detector efficiency, charge-sharing, and fluorescence-escape effects—all of which can vary across the narrow above/below-edge window and are particularly relevant for CdTe detectors near 80 keV—do not cancel in the simple ratio and would need to be characterized or corrected. Subject to these corrections, a spatially varying edge-jump map would translate into a spatially varying thickness map of the sputtered layer, which might reveal the deposition footprint and any thickness gradients characteristic of sputtered coatings (often thicker near the center of the deposition zone and thinner toward the edges). This expected pattern is a hypothesis, not an observed result.

### Confidence and Caveats

The physical model rests on a single, element-specific spectral feature rather than a full spectral decomposition, which is a strength in principle. However, several factors currently limit confidence, and—importantly—no data (I0 spectrum, absorbance spectrum, edge-jump map, or thickness map) has yet been presented or verified. The primary sources of uncertainty are: (1) the photon flux available above ~80.7 keV, which sets counting statistics and must be confirmed from the actual I0 spectrum; (2) the detector's energy resolution—a value of 0.2 keV was previously stated, but this is far better than typical Hexitec CdTe detectors (which are commonly ~1–2 keV FWHM at these energies), so the true resolution must be verified, as it governs how sharply the 80.7 keV step can be resolved; (3) partial-only cancellation of detector-response effects in the edge ratio (see above); (4) potential interference from tungsten characteristic lines near the normalization window; and (5) pixel-to-pixel variation in the flat-field reference. For very thin sputtered layers the edge jump may approach the noise floor, so any thickness estimates in the thinnest regions would carry lower confidence. Given that no edge-jump map or measured absorbance step above noise has been demonstrated, this work should be regarded as a proposed methodology rather than a validated result; confidence in successfully locating and mapping the gold must remain provisional until an actual edge-jump map and quantitative validation are provided.

### Unified Physical Picture

If the proposed approach is validated, the sample would be expected to be describable as a spatially confined sputtered gold film on an otherwise low-attenuation substrate, localized wherever the ~80.7 keV absorption step appears, with local thickness encoded in the height of that step. The flat-field reference would underpin the measurement by removing source and instrument signatures, allowing the gold K-edge to be read quantitatively. The anticipated outcome—a well-defined gold region with a smoothly varying thickness profile consistent with sputter-deposition geometry—is a hypothesis to be tested against data that have not yet been shown.

### Key Evidence
- **I0 flat-field baseline cube (no sample) on the same grid (spatial-mean spectrum)**: This reference is intended to define the incident bremsstrahlung beam profile, including its low-energy rise, mid-energy continuum, and tungsten characteristic emission lines. It would serve as the essential normalization operand to convert raw sample transmission into absorbance. Note: the I0 spectrum has not been shown or verified here, so its detailed shape, endpoint energy, above-edge flux at ~80.7 keV, and the position of tungsten K-lines relative to the Au K-edge window all remain to be confirmed. No images (I0 spectrum, absorbance spectrum, edge-jump map, or thickness map) are available for verification.

scientific_claims.claim: The spatial distribution and local thickness of a sputtered gold film could, in principle, be mapped by measuring the magnitude of the characteristic Au K-edge absorption jump (~80.7 keV) in energy-resolved X-ray transmission images, provided detector-response effects are corrected and sufficient above-edge flux is confirmed.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: If validated with actual edge-jump and thickness maps, establishing that a single element-specific absorption edge yields quantitative, spatially resolved thickness maps would support spectral X-ray imaging as a non-destructive metrology tool for thin metallic coatings, complementing techniques such as X-ray fluorescence and profilometry.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone quantified the thickness of a sputtered metal film by mapping the height of its characteristic X-ray absorption K-edge jump in energy-resolved transmission imaging?

scientific_claims.claim: Normalizing sample transmission spectra by a matched flat-field reference cube is intended to isolate element-specific absorption edges from the underlying bremsstrahlung source structure; however, complete removal of source/detector signatures near 80 keV is not guaranteed, as tungsten characteristic lines and energy-dependent detector-response effects may persist and require explicit correction.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Demonstrating that per-pixel flat-field normalization reliably removes source and detector signatures—once detector-response and characteristic-line effects are properly accounted for—would strengthen the quantitative reliability of energy-resolved photon-counting detectors for elemental mapping and areal-density measurements.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone used per-pixel flat-field normalization of energy-resolved X-ray transmission data to isolate absorption edges from bremsstrahlung source features for quantitative elemental mapping?

dynamic_analysis_records.target: For each pixel, form the per-pixel transmission by dividing the sample cube by the same-grid I0 flat-field cube (gating out low-flux/zero-I0 pixels and ignoring energies below 5 keV), then take -ln(I/I0) to get absorbance. Measure the Au K-edge jump at 80.8 keV using the edge-step helper (measure_edge_step) so robust pre-/post-edge windows and flux gating are handled by the tool; record whether the edge is measurable. Produce a spatial map of the Au K-edge step to locate the Au. Then convert the measured edge step to Au thickness via the Beer-Lambert law using the change in mass attenuation coefficient across the Au K-edge obtained from the attenuation helper for elemental Au (do not hard-code attenuation values). Output a per-pixel Au thickness map. Mask/flag pixels where the edge is not measurable rather than reporting spurious thickness.

def analyze_feature(data, axis, auxiliary=None):
    import scipy.ndimage as ndi
    from scilink.skills._shared.edge_step import measure_edge_step
    from scilink.skills._shared.xray_attenuation import attenuation

    energy = np.asarray(axis, dtype=float)
    cube = np.asarray(data, dtype=float)
    H, W, E = cube.shape
    edge_kev = 80.8

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Obtain a TRUE open-beam I0 flat-field. Do NOT fabricate one.
    #    If no genuine I0 is supplied, the K-edge transmission method is
    #    not applicable -> flag everything as not measurable.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    i0 = None
    if auxiliary:
        for k in auxiliary:
            if 'I0' in k or 'flat' in k.lower() or 'baseline' in k.lower():
                cand = np.asarray(auxiliary[k], dtype=float)
                if cand.shape == cube.shape:
                    i0 = cand
                    break

    nan_map = np.full((H, W), np.nan, dtype=float)
    zeros_map = np.zeros((H, W), dtype=float)

    if i0 is None:
        # No genuine open-beam reference: refuse to fabricate transmission.
        return {
            "maps": {
                "Au_Edge_Step": nan_map.copy(),
                "Au_Thickness": nan_map.copy(),
                "Measurable_Mask": zeros_map.copy(),
                "Edge_SNR": nan_map.copy(),
            },
            "units": {
                "Au_Edge_Step": "delta-OD (unitless)",
                "Au_Thickness": "micrometers",
                "Measurable_Mask": "boolean (0/1)",
                "Edge_SNR": "unitless",
            },
            "description": (
                "No genuine open-beam I0 flat-field cube was supplied. A true "
                "open-beam reference is REQUIRED to form transmission T=I/I0 and "
                "measure the Au K-edge step. Self-normalization against the sample "
                "field median only re-encodes the beam/detector spatial flux profile "
                "as a spurious edge and is refused. All outputs are flagged as "
                "NOT MEASURABLE (NaN / mask=0)."
            ),
        }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Honest measurability check on the FIELD-MEAN spectrum BEFORE any
    #    per-pixel fitting. Check whether the K-edge region carries flux
    #    and whether a step actually exists in the field-mean OD.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Light spectral smoothing only for diagnostics / stability (does not
    # erase a real edge which is broad on this coarse energy grid).
    smooth_cube = ndi.uniform_filter1d(cube, size=3, axis=-1, mode='nearest')
    smooth_i0 = ndi.uniform_filter1d(i0, size=3, axis=-1, mode='nearest')

    # Continuum windows just below/above the edge (wide, feature-local).
    pre_lo, pre_hi = edge_kev - 6.0, edge_kev - 2.0
    post_lo, post_hi = edge_kev + 1.0, edge_kev + 5.0
    pre_sel = (energy >= pre_lo) & (energy < pre_hi)
    post_sel = (energy >= post_lo) & (energy < post_hi)

    # Field-mean incident flux in the post-edge window (photons available).
    field_i0 = i0.reshape(-1, E).mean(axis=0)
    post_flux_field = np.nanmedian(field_i0[post_sel]) if post_sel.any() else 0.0

    # A coarse, honest flux floor: the K-edge tail is often photon-starved.
    FLUX_FLOOR = 20.0

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Use the registered edge-step helper (robust windows + flux gate).
    #    It reports whether the edge is measurable rather than fabricating.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    edge_step_map = nan_map.copy()
    snr_map = nan_map.copy()
    measurable_mask = zeros_map.copy()
    thickness_map = nan_map.copy()

    try:
        r = measure_edge_step(
            data=cube,
            i0=i0,
            energy_kev=energy,
            edge_kev=edge_kev,
            pre_gap=2.0,
            post_gap=1.0,
            win_width=4.0,
            low_e_cut_kev=5.0,
            flux_floor_counts=FLUX_FLOOR,
            auto_center=True,
            search_tol_kev=2.0,
        )
    except Exception:
        r = None

    field_measurable = bool(r['measurable']) if (r is not None and 'measurable' in r) else False
    # Extra guard: require genuine post-edge flux in the field mean.
    if post_flux_field < FLUX_FLOOR:
        field_measurable = False

    if r is not None and field_measurable:
        es = np.asarray(r['edge_step'], dtype=float)
        snr = np.asarray(r['snr'], dtype=float)
        if es.shape == (H, W):
            edge_step_map = es
            snr_map = snr

            # Per-pixel measurability: require SNR > 3 (helper guidance).
            pix_ok = np.isfinite(snr) & (snr > 3.0) & np.isfinite(es)
            # A K-edge jump is a POSITIVE step in optical depth.
            pix_ok &= (es > 0.0)
            measurable_mask = pix_ok.astype(float)

            # ----------------------------------------------------------
            # 4. Beer-Lambert: convert delta-OD to Au thickness using the
            #    CHANGE in mass attenuation across the K-edge, from the
            #    attenuation helper (no hard-coded mu values).
            # ----------------------------------------------------------
            # Sample mu/rho just below and just above the edge.
            e_below = np.array([edge_kev - 0.8])
            e_above = np.array([edge_kev + 0.8])
            mu_below = float(attenuation('Au', e_below)[0])   # cm^2/g
            mu_above = float(attenuation('Au', e_above)[0])   # cm^2/g
            dmu = abs(mu_above - mu_below)                     # cm^2/g
            rho_au = 19.32                                     # g/cm^3

            if dmu > 1e-6:
                # delta-OD = dmu * rho * t  ->  t[cm] = dOD/(dmu*rho)
                t_cm = es / (dmu * rho_au)
                t_um = t_cm * 1e4  # cm -> micrometers
                # Only report thickness where the edge is measurable.
                t_out = np.full((H, W), np.nan, dtype=float)
                good = pix_ok & (t_um >= 0)
                t_out[good] = t_um[good]
                thickness_map = t_out

    # If nothing was measurable, keep NaN/zeros (honest flagging).
    n_ok = int(np.nansum(measurable_mask))

    desc = (
        "Per-pixel Au K-edge (80.8 keV) analysis via true open-beam transmission. "
        "Transmission T=I/I0 formed from the supplied flat-field cube; measure_edge_step "
        "handles robust pre-/post-edge continuum windows, low-energy cut (5 keV) and a "
        "photon-flux gate. The field-mean post-edge flux was checked FIRST: if the K-edge "
        "region is photon-starved (post-edge I0 below the flux floor) the edge is declared "
        "NOT MEASURABLE and no thickness is fabricated. Edge_Step = delta optical depth; "
        "pixels with SNR<=3 or non-positive step are masked. Thickness from Beer-Lambert: "
        "t = delta-OD / (delta(mu/rho) * rho_Au), with delta(mu/rho) taken across the K-edge "
        "from the attenuation helper (no hard-coded values) and rho_Au=19.32 g/cm^3. "
        f"Measurable pixels: {n_ok}. "
    )
    if n_ok == 0:
        desc += (
            "WARNING: zero pixels passed the measurability gate -- the 80.8 keV K-edge "
            "sits in a photon-starved tail of this spectrum. The Au signal is likely only "
            "accessible via the Au L-edges (~11.9-14.4 keV) or fluorescence lines in the "
            "high-flux region; the K-edge thickness map is intentionally NaN rather than spurious."
        )

    return {
        "maps": {
            "Au_Edge_Step": edge_step_map,
            "Au_Thickness": thickness_map,
            "Measurable_Mask": measurable_mask,
            "Edge_SNR": snr_map,
        },
        "units": {
            "Au_Edge_Step": "delta-OD (unitless)",
            "Au_Thickness": "micrometers",
            "Measurable_Mask": "boolean (0/1)",
            "Edge_SNR": "unitless",
        },
        "description": desc,
    }

issues.problem: Two linked, specific flaws make this result an artifact rather than a sputtered-Au measurement. (1) BROKEN REFERENCE: no real open-beam I0 flat-field is available, so the code silently falls back to a pseudo-I0 = median spectrum across all pixels. This measures OD as a deviation from the average pixel, not absolute transmission. The Au_Edge_Step map is a smooth, monotonic top→bright / bottom→masked gradient across the 20 mm field — this is the signature of the beam/detector-flux profile (and the flux gate failing where counts fall below the floor), NOT the morphology of a sputtered Au coupon. The mean spectrum confirms the physics: strong W-tube characteristic lines at ~59/67 keV and a steeply falling continuum through 70–90 keV, with no clear absorption step visible at 80.8 keV; near the Au K-edge the flux is already ~100 counts and dropping, so the bottom-of-field masking is flux starvation, not real Au absence. (2) PHYSICALLY ABSURD VALUE: converting the mean ΔOD≈0.92 (up to ~2.0) via Beer-Lambert with Δ(μ/ρ)≈6.7 cm²/g and ρ=19.32 g/cm³ gives t≈70 µm (up to ~160 µm). A sputtered Au film is nm-to-~µm scale; 70 µm is 1–2 orders of magnitude too thick and unattainable by sputtering — a clear signal that the extracted ΔOD is dominated by the pseudo-I0/beam-profile artifact rather than a real K-edge jump. Corrective direction: supply/derive a genuine open-beam I0 flat-field (or an unattenuated region-of-interest normalization) before forming T=I/I0; if no true I0 exists, the edge-step-to-thickness conversion is not defensible. Also verify a discernible 80.8 keV step exists per-pixel above the flux floor before reporting thickness, and sanity-bound the thickness against sputtering-plausible scales.

Two fatal problems converge here. (1) NO REAL I0: the code's I0 fallback uses the median spectrum of the cube itself as a pseudo-flat-field, so T=I/I0 is a self-normalization, not a true transmission. The Au K-edge step measured against this is not a physical Delta-OD. (2) The mean spectrum shows essentially NO photons above ~85 keV — counts fall to near-zero well before the 80.8 keV Au K-edge and the continuum is buried in noise by 100 keV. At 80.8 keV there is negligible flux, so any 'edge step' extracted is photon-starved noise, not a measurable K-edge. The result confirms this: the thickness map is a smooth top-to-bottom gradient (0-160 um) that mirrors the beam/geometry falloff rather than a localized sputtered layer, and the physically implausible values (mean 73 um, up to 163 um of Au — sputtered Au layers are typically sub-micron to a few um) are the tell. A sputtered Au film would be nanometers-to-microns thick with a K-edge jump far too small to detect at this flux; the gradient + tens-of-microns thicknesses are the fingerprint of fitting a phantom edge to the falling bremsstrahlung tail against a self-derived I0. Corrective direction: this measurement cannot be done as posed — the Au K-edge at 80.8 keV has insufficient flux in this dataset. Either (a) require a genuine measured I0 flat-field (not the cube median) and re-run measure_edge_step, and if the field-level measurable flag then fails, report that the edge is not detectable; or (b) if the sputtered Au is thin, locate it instead via the Au L-edges (~11.9/13.7/14.4 keV) or the Au L-fluorescence lines (Lalpha ~9.7 keV) which sit in the high-flux region of this spectrum, rather than the flux-starved K-edge.

The histogram's large spike at exactly 0 plus a broad high-value lobe is consistent with a gradient being thresholded, not a discrete film edge. CORRECTIVE DIRECTION: The measurement requires a genuine open-beam I0 flat-field cube to form absolute transmission; the reported result implies the code proceeded with a self-derived/pseudo-I0 (the earlier failure mode) or an I0 that does not remove the source flux profile.
